## Spectral Analysis

The experimental peaks and their structural implications:

**Key peaks to explain:**
- 1004 cm⁻¹ (strongest) — classic monosubstituted benzene ring breathing mode
- 1600 cm⁻¹ (strongest) — aromatic C=C stretching
- 1700 cm⁻¹ (strongest) — C=O stretch (aldehyde)
- 1206 cm⁻¹ — C-H in-plane bending / C-C stretch
- 830 cm⁻¹ — aromatic C-H out-of-plane bending
- 1167 cm⁻¹ — aromatic C-H in-plane bending
- 3073 cm⁻¹ — aromatic/aldehyde C-H stretch
- 619 cm⁻¹ — ring out-of-plane deformation
- 1024 cm⁻¹ — ring in-plane C-H bending
- 653 cm⁻¹ — ring deformation

**Structural assignment:**

The dominant 1004 cm⁻¹ band is the hallmark of a **monosubstituted benzene** (benzaldehyde-type), corresponding to the symmetric ring breathing mode. Candidate 1 (benzaldehyde, `O=Cc1ccccc1`) has exactly this monosubstituted pattern.

The 1700 cm⁻¹ peak confirms an aldehyde C=O stretch. The 1600 cm⁻¹ peak is the aromatic ring C=C stretch. The 830 cm⁻¹ band is consistent with para-disubstituted benzene out-of-plane C-H wag in some cases, but for monosubstituted benzene it can also appear in this region.

**Ruling out other candidates:**
- Candidates 2–4 (chloro/fluoro-substituted benzaldehydes) are para-disubstituted; their ring breathing mode shifts away from 1004 cm⁻¹ and the 830 cm⁻¹ band would be stronger/more prominent as a para-substitution marker.
- Candidates 5–10 contain additional heteroatoms, sulfur groups, or non-aromatic frameworks that would introduce extra peaks not present here.

The clean set of monosubstituted benzene ring modes (1004, 1600, 1206, 1167, 1024, 619 cm⁻¹) together with the aldehyde carbonyl at 1700 cm⁻¹ and aromatic C-H stretch at 3073 cm⁻¹ is a textbook match for **benzaldehyde**.

SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.88
EXPLANATION: The 1004 cm⁻¹ band is the definitive monosubstituted benzene ring breathing mode, uniquely consistent with benzaldehyde (candidate 1). Combined with the 1700 cm⁻¹ aldehyde C=O stretch, 1600 cm⁻¹ aromatic C=C stretch, 3073 cm⁻¹ aromatic C-H stretch, and the full set of benzene ring deformation modes (619, 830, 1024, 1167, 1206 cm⁻¹), the spectrum matches benzaldehyde with no unexplained peaks and no missing expected peaks. Para-disubstituted candidates (2–4) would shift the ring breathing mode and strengthen the 830 cm⁻¹ band disproportionately; more complex candidates (5–10) would introduce sulfur or other heteroatom modes not observed.
